stories.t: Gunfire at a Fairfield Halloween store leaves one dead and six hurt
stories.s: Police say a gunman opened fire inside a Spirit Halloween store at Solano Town Center on Friday around 8:30 p.m., killing one person and wounding six. At least three of the injured were in critical condition, and no arrest had been reported. Detectives are interviewing witnesses and asking anyone with information to call Fairfield police.
stories.w: Fairfield is about an hour’s drive from the Peninsula, and the shooting happened during a holiday weekend when stores and events draw crowds across the Bay Area.

stories.t: Analysis: 42% of names on DOJ’s “likely noncitizen” list aren’t on California’s voter rolls
stories.s: Two UCLA data scientists reviewed the list the Trump administration sent California in early October and found that 8,880 of its roughly 21,000 names do not appear in the state’s current voter files. The analysis was filed in court Saturday by an immigrant-rights group and a candidate for governor, who argue that many eligible citizens were wrongly flagged. A federal appeals court ruled against the administration’s complaint a second time on Friday.
stories.w: With Election Day on Tuesday, the fight over this list affects whether flagged voters in San Mateo County and across California have their ballots counted.

stories.t: Daylight saving time ends: set clocks back an hour
stories.s: Clocks “fall back” this weekend as daylight saving time ends, giving most people an extra hour of sleep. A sleep specialist interviewed by CBS News offers tips for easing the adjustment, which can leave some people groggy for a few days.
stories.w: Phones update on their own, but stove, car and wall clocks do not, and darker evenings arrive just as commutes on Caltrain and BART shift back toward dusk.

stories.t: Valkyries win the WNBA title in Game 7 for the franchise’s first championship
stories.s: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68–63 on Saturday in San Francisco, winning the title in just their second season. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, 28 of them in the second half, and was named Finals MVP. A championship parade runs along the Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 4, with fans able to line up from 9 a.m.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors rest Curry, 49ers regroup on a bye, Quakes are playoff-bound
stories.s: The Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 on Friday, with Stephen Curry scoring 31, and play the Clippers on Sunday without him: the team says he is sitting out for injury management because of a lingering knee issue. The 49ers are on a bye after last week’s 29–20 loss in Atlanta. The San Jose Earthquakes have already clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs, which begin Nov. 18, and were fourth in the West when they clinched.

stories.t: 49ers add DeForest Buckner, but a trade for Jauan Jennings fell through
stories.s: San Francisco recently acquired two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Newsweek, citing a Fox Sports report, says the team also worked out terms for Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings, but he declined to say he wanted to return and the deal died. Coach Kyle Shanahan has said receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson could be back after the bye.

stories.t: NFL fines 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw $12,537 for a punch at a Falcons receiver
stories.s: The league fined Greenlaw for a punch aimed at the ball that instead landed on Atlanta receiver Drake London’s head in the Week 7 loss. Reports say it is his second fine of the season.

stories.t: Netflix renews “The Diplomat” for a fifth season
stories.s: Netflix confirmed Thursday that the political thriller starring Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell will return, two weeks after season four debuted on Oct. 15. The show has spent 13 weeks in Netflix’s global Top 10. No release date or story details have been announced yet.

stories.t: Next up on streaming: “Black Doves,” “Rings of Power” and “12 12 12”
stories.s: November’s early premieres include season two of the British spy series “Black Doves” on Netflix on Nov. 5 and season three of “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” on Prime Video on Nov. 11, with four episodes at once and weekly releases after. Apple TV+ launches the crime-thriller miniseries “12 12 12” on Nov. 13.

stories.t: NASA asks industry how to lift Hubble into a safer orbit
stories.s: NASA issued a request for information asking companies how they could raise, service or safely bring down the Hubble Space Telescope, aiming for a mission by 2032 that would lift it to at least 600 kilometers. Without help, Hubble is expected to fall back to Earth in the early-to-mid 2030s. NASA says it is only gathering ideas and has not committed to paying for a rescue.

stories.t: Mistral publishes the weights of its trillion-parameter Large 4 model
stories.s: The French AI company released the downloadable weights for Mistral Large 4, so companies and governments can run it on their own systems. It is pitched at cybersecurity work and coding agents, and Mistral says it matches a leading Chinese open model while using 47 percent fewer tokens per task. The weights are on Hugging Face and the model is also available through Mistral’s API.

stories.t: Four-person crew finishes a 378-day simulated Mars mission
stories.s: NASA’s second CHAPEA crew stepped out of a 3D-printed habitat at Johnson Space Center on Saturday after more than a year of isolation. The four volunteers grew crops in simulated Martian soil and worked with limited resources and communication delays, so researchers can learn how astronauts stay healthy on long trips.

stories.t: Data centers and AI become a midterm issue, even in Brooklyn
stories.s: At a political event five days before Election Day, conversation kept returning to AI and data centers, according to TechCrunch. A recent industry report found nearly $200 billion of data center projects were delayed or blocked in the first half of 2026 amid local opposition.

stories.t: Layoffs pile up as October ends, including cuts in San Francisco
stories.s: Companies announcing cuts this week included Comcast, Amazon’s devices unit, Disney’s theme parks, and Alaska Air Group, which plans about 200 non-contract job cuts including 48 in Hawaii. In San Francisco, state notices list 57 jobs at Dropbox and 53 at Front, and a Levy operation in Oakland will close Dec. 31 with 181 workers affected.
stories.w: Bay Area tech cuts are small but steady, a sign of a tougher local job market heading into the holidays.

stories.t: Tech money makes up at least a fifth of outside spending in California legislative races
stories.s: Spending on Assembly and Senate races topped $128 million as of Oct. 29, up from $74 million in 2022, and groups funded by Google, Meta, and other tech interests account for at least 20% of contributions to outside spenders. Unlike candidate donations, which are capped at $5,900, these independent expenditures have no limit.
stories.w: Outside money is shaping the people who will write California’s rules on AI, data centers, and tech jobs that matter to Peninsula workers.

stories.t: Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 to reach .500
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Lakers 112–95 on Friday at Chase Center in an NBA Cup game for their third straight win, evening their record at 3–3; they host the Clippers on Sunday. 49ers: 6–1, back from their bye next week. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Halloween night sky: Saturn and early fireballs
stories.s: Around 7 p.m., look east-southeast for Saturn, a bright yellow-white point about two fists above the horizon; a small telescope shows its nearly edge-on rings. Early Taurid meteors, the so-called Halloween fireballs, can streak from the east-northeast, with the shower peaking in the second week of November.

stories.t: China’s secretive space plane is visible before dawn this week
stories.s: Shenlong, China’s reusable space plane on its fourth mission, can be seen as a steady moving point of light in the predawn sky. In California, a good pass is expected over Los Angeles early on Nov. 2; Bay Area skywatchers can find local times on Heavens-Above.

stories.t: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Rosalind for life sciences research
stories.s: OpenAI released GPT-6 Rosalind, a model built for biological reasoning and scientific tool use. Access is limited to approved organizations through the company’s trusted-access program for research.

stories.t: Halloween weekend brings a coastal flood advisory and a chance of drizzle
stories.s: A coastal flood advisory covers shoreline areas of San Francisco and San Pablo bays through 6 p.m. Sunday, with up to 1.9 feet of water possible in low spots. Rain spreads into the Bay Area later Saturday, so trick-or-treaters may see light drizzle, with highs in the low 60s.
stories.w: Plan Halloween routes away from flood-prone bayside streets near high tide, and bring a light rain layer for kids.

stories.t: Could Prop. 45 open the door to more California data centers?
stories.s: Prop. 45 is pitched as a pro-housing overhaul of environmental review, but legal scholars say its streamlining for telecom and support infrastructure could let data centers sidestep a new state law. Supporters, who have raised more than $40 million including $3 million from PG&E, say data centers aren’t covered, and at least 26 cities and counties have moved to limit them.
stories.w: Data centers draw heavily on the power grid and water, which affects utility bills and local planning on the Peninsula.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors host the Lakers in an NBA Cup game
stories.s: Warriors: 2–3 after Wednesday’s 119–114 win at Minnesota; they host the Lakers tonight at Chase Center in an NBA Cup game. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: trimming the roster ahead of the off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: New this weekend: Apple TV’s Nocturne and Dexter: Resurrection season 2
stories.s: Apple TV premieres Nocturne with two episodes, starring Liev Schreiber as a soldier turned homicide detective and Stephen Graham as a serial killer, and also airs the Dark Matter season 2 finale. Paramount+ launches the second season of Dexter: Resurrection, and the Daytime Emmys stream tonight.

stories.t: New music Friday: THAO, Sampa the Great, DIIV, and Queens of the Stone Age
stories.s: THAO’s Show Me is a personal record about divorce and change, and Sampa the Great’s Nu Zamrock blends Zambia’s 1970s Zamrock sound with hip-hop and soul. DIIV teams with producer A.G. Cook on the glossier ZIRP!, and Queens of the Stone Age also have a new album out.

stories.t: Astronauts mark the 100th US spacewalk from the space station
stories.s: NASA’s Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk spent 7 hours and 11 minutes outside the station installing an upgraded solar array that unrolled to 63 feet on its own. It was the first spacewalk by a Canadian since 2019, and the pair go out again Nov. 5 to add the last new array.

stories.t: Virgin Galactic’s new space plane flies for the first time
stories.s: Apeiron, the first of Virgin Galactic’s Delta-class ships, flew beneath its carrier plane from Arizona to Spaceport America in New Mexico for testing. The company plans to start carrying paying customers in spring 2027, with nearly 700 ticket holders waiting.

stories.t: ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can claim up to $500 a month in API credits
stories.s: OpenAI says eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can now claim up to $500 a month in free API credits by linking an API organization they own, making it cheaper to try building with OpenAI’s models.

stories.t: Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% as two officials push for a hike
stories.s: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged after September’s increase, with Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook dissenting in favor of another quarter-point hike. The statement gave no clear signal about December, as inflation ran at 3.7% in September and energy prices stay high.
stories.w: Steady but high rates keep mortgages, car loans, and credit cards expensive in one of the country’s priciest housing markets.

stories.t: Judge refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots
stories.s: US District Judge David O. Carter rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside ballots from voters it says might not be citizens, citing a pattern of attempted election interference. Prosecutors conceded some people on the federal list are likely citizens, and the administration plans to appeal.
stories.w: San Mateo County ballots are counted under the same state rules, so the ruling keeps local counting on its normal track.

stories.t: High-speed rail chief resigns amid a travel spending scandal
stories.s: Ian Choudri stepped down as CEO of the California High-Speed Rail Authority, effective immediately, after reports that nearly $600,000 went to questionable consultant trips. State Finance Director Joe Stephenshaw takes over a project now estimated at $126 billion to $231 billion.
stories.w: The Peninsula is part of the planned San Francisco-to-Los Angeles route, sharing Caltrain’s corridor.

stories.t: Measure V asks San Mateo County voters to extend an $848 million college bond
stories.s: The bond would fund a new gym, arts building upgrades, and repairs at Cañada College, College of San Mateo, and Skyline College, extending an existing tax of $18 per $100,000 of assessed value through 2049. Critics point to a past bribery scandal tied to earlier bond contracts, which led to a former chancellor’s jail sentence.
stories.w: A median-priced county home would pay about $386 a year, and Skyline and CSM are the closest campuses to Millbrae.

stories.t: Curry scores 44 as the Warriors win at Minnesota
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Timberwolves 119–114 on Wednesday behind 44 points from Stephen Curry; Jonathan Kuminga led Minnesota with 20. Golden State is 2–3 and hosts the Lakers on Friday. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Giants start a pivotal off-season with pitching at the top of the list
stories.s: San Francisco finished with 24 players on the injured list and must trim to 40-man roster limits within days. The front office wants at least two starters behind Logan Webb and Landen Roupp plus a closer, and may try to trade a big contract, all before a possible lockout on Dec. 1.

stories.t: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek’s Captain Picard, dies at 86
stories.s: Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, his spokesperson said. He played Jean-Luc Picard across seven seasons, four films, and Star Trek: Picard, and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, alongside a celebrated Shakespearean stage career.

stories.t: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, starting with cybersecurity defenders
stories.s: Google calls Gemini 4 Carbon its strongest model for long, multi-step engineering work and cybersecurity tasks such as finding and patching vulnerabilities. Access starts with a group of cyber defenders, and Google says developers, businesses, and consumers will get it after more feedback and safety work.

stories.t: SpaceX test-fires Starship ahead of Flight 15
stories.s: SpaceX completed static fires of Ship 42, including a full-duration burn of all six engines, after testing the Super Heavy booster that will fly with it. Elon Musk is targeting November for Flight 15 and wants to try catching both the ship and the booster, pending approval.

stories.t: About $164 million has flowed through Mayor Lurie’s political and charity network
stories.s: The San Francisco Standard tallied roughly $124 million in private donations to city efforts and $39 million in political money tied to Lurie since 2023, plus $10 million of his own in 2024. Four November measures he backs, including three charter reforms and a Muni parcel tax, have raised $18.6 million.
stories.w: Many Peninsula commuters rely on Muni and BART connections in the city, so the San Francisco measures on this ballot shape regional transit too.

stories.t: Most California Republicans in Congress skip a pledge to seat election winners
stories.s: A bipartisan pledge to oppose efforts to undermine free and fair elections has 17 signers, including five California Democrats. Rep. Kevin Kiley, now an independent, was the only member of California’s Republican delegation to sign; several others did not respond. The pledge aims to head off a repeat of the pressure on Congress after the 2020 election.
stories.w: With the House majority razor-thin, how California’s representatives handle certification could matter for the whole country.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors visit Minnesota tonight
stories.s: Warriors: 1–3 after Monday’s 134–114 win at Denver; they play at Minnesota tonight. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Final Dune: Part Three trailer lands ahead of a Dec. 18 release
stories.s: The last trailer for Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three, starring Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya, leans into war on Arrakis and Paul’s turn toward tyranny, with a bigger role for Chani than in the novel. The film opens in theaters only on Dec. 18, the same holiday stretch as Avengers: Doomsday.

stories.t: Astronomers spot a possible new dwarf planet beyond Neptune
stories.s: Data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory revealed 2026 ED138, an object estimated at 600 to 1,500 kilometers across about 46 times farther from the sun than Earth. If its size is confirmed, likely with infrared telescopes such as JWST, it would become the sixth known dwarf planet.

stories.t: GitHub Copilot Fusion picks the AI model for each request
stories.s: Instead of choosing a model yourself, Copilot Fusion routes each prompt, sometimes drafting with a lighter model and escalating or having a second model review the work. It is available on all Copilot plans in VS Code, the GitHub CLI, and JetBrains tools, with a temporary 30% discount for paid users.

stories.t: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
stories.s: Microsoft offered a voluntary exit package to roughly a quarter of its workforce at level 70 and below in the US, Canada, India, and the UK, with each business unit deciding whether to take part. Those who accept leave by year-end with standard severance, and the company said layoffs remain possible.
stories.w: Microsoft is a major Bay Area employer, and big-tech buyouts ripple through local hiring and the housing market.

stories.t: King tides flood bayside roads, with more high water due this week
stories.s: High tides swamped parts of Marin on Monday, flooding a Highway 101 off-ramp and stranding drivers and pedestrians until the water receded. A coastal flood advisory for low-lying shoreline areas runs through Thursday afternoon, with San Francisco’s highest tides about 2 feet above normal around midday today.
stories.w: Bayfront areas along the Peninsula, including near Millbrae and Burlingame, can see the same midday flooding, so avoid shoreline paths and low roads around high tide.

stories.t: California’s last-minute voting guide: mail ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3
stories.s: Mail ballots count if they are postmarked by Election Day and arrive within seven days, and early voting centers are open in every county. The ballot carries 14 statewide propositions, including Prop. 40, which would make California the first state with a billionaire tax, plus races for governor and several competitive House seats.
stories.w: Peninsula voters can still mail a ballot, drop it off, or vote in person at any San Mateo County vote center through Election Day.

stories.t: A river otter returns to the San Mateo coast after more than 100 years
stories.s: Wildlife cameras in a closed area of the Cloverdale Ranch preserve near Pescadero caught a North American river otter this summer, the first documented on the San Mateo coast since the 1800s. Biologists say the otter, which needs clean water and plenty of food, is a sign the creeks there are healthy.
stories.w: It’s a hopeful sign for the county’s coastal creeks, which also support coho salmon and steelhead.

stories.t: Warriors earn their first win, routing Denver 134–114
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Nuggets 134–114 on Monday for their first win; Yaxel Lendeborg scored 31. Golden State is 1–3 and plays at Minnesota on Wednesday. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Star Trek’s Walter Koenig, who played Chekov, dies at 90
stories.s: Koenig died Sunday at his home in North Hollywood. He played navigator Pavel Chekov in 36 episodes of the original Star Trek and in the first seven films, and later played Alfred Bester on Babylon 5. He also wrote two memoirs about his career.

stories.t: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster model for writing and computer use
stories.s: OpenAI added GPT-6.1 Terra to its API, describing it as a fast, efficient model built for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing. It is available now to developers, with migration guidance in the company’s GPT-6 guide.

stories.t: San Mateo County urges early storm prep as a strong El Niño grows likely
stories.s: NOAA puts the odds of a strong to very strong El Niño this winter above 83%, and county leaders worry most about storms that line up with high tides or hit already soaked hillsides. After declaring a local emergency, the county is clearing drains and culverts, mapping sandbag sites, and forming a task force that may include Caltrans and PG&E. Residents can sign up for emergency alerts through SMC Alert.
stories.w: Millbrae’s hillside streets and bayfront flats face both landslide and flood risk, so now is the time to clear gutters, check insurance, and sign up for alerts.

stories.t: 49ers’ unbeaten run ends with a 29–20 loss in Atlanta
stories.s: 49ers: lost 29–20 at the Falcons on Sunday despite outgaining Atlanta 400 yards to 295; four turnovers proved costly, and Christian McCaffrey had 100 total yards and a touchdown. San Francisco is 6–1 and heads into its bye week. Warriors: 0–3, play at Denver tonight. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: New this week: The Mob on Hulu and Netflix’s Minimum Wage
stories.s: Hulu premieres The Mob, a reality competition hosted by Parker Posey and set in an Italian villa with up to $250,000 on the line. Netflix drops all 14 episodes of Minimum Wage, and Peacock opens its second season of NBA Monday with the Warriors at the Nuggets.

stories.t: October’s Hunter’s Moon peaks overnight
stories.s: The full moon reached peak illumination at 9:12 p.m. Pacific on Sunday, so it will still look full when it rises in the east around sunset tonight. The name comes from the bare, harvested fields of fall, when hunters once had an easier time spotting game.

stories.t: US pulls diplomats from Middle East posts after warning of Iranian plots
stories.s: The State Department ordered non-emergency staff and all family members out of Saudi Arabia and quietly reduced staffing in Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar, and Jordan. An Oct. 23 intelligence memo said Iranian efforts to target US personnel have reached “advanced stages.” A union for foreign service officers called the moves chaotic.
stories.w: Renewed conflict could push oil and gas prices higher again, and anyone with family or travel plans in the region should check State Department advisories.

stories.t: Seven more San Mateo County vote centers open ahead of Nov. 3
stories.s: New vote centers opened Saturday in Burlingame, Daly City, East Palo Alto, Half Moon Bay, Pacifica, Redwood City, and San Carlos, joining three that have been open since early October. All 10 are open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily through Nov. 2, and 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3.
stories.w: Burlingame’s new center is the closest to Millbrae, which has no vote center of its own.

stories.t: California voters face about $44 billion in bond measures
stories.s: Three propositions add up to roughly $44 billion: Prop. 1 is an $11.25 billion affordable housing bond expected to create about 40,000 rental units, Prop. 38 funds immunology research, and Prop. 37 helps new-home buyers with down payments through private lenders. The state already spends about $6 billion a year paying off past bonds.
stories.w: Housing bonds shape how much affordable housing gets built on the Peninsula, and all state bonds are repaid from the general fund over decades.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors drop a second straight; 49ers face the Falcons
stories.s: Warriors: lost 131–122 at Phoenix on Saturday as Devin Booker scored 43; Yaxel Lendeborg led Golden State with 26 and hit six 3-pointers. 49ers: play the Falcons today. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: 49ers activate Christian Kirk as Evans and Samuel sit out
stories.s: San Francisco activated Christian Kirk off injured reserve, and he is set to make his 49ers debut today. With Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel ruled out, the team has just four receivers: Kirk, Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing. The 49ers also called up two practice-squad players for the game.

stories.t: Jung Hoo Lee calls 2026 a ‘rollercoaster season’ as Giants weigh the outfield
stories.s: Lee set career highs with a .276 average, 10 home runs, and 57 RBIs, but cooled sharply over his final 55 games after a strong first half. Manager Tony Vitello expects another step forward. With 10 outfielders on the depth chart, the Giants could trade from that surplus, though Lee’s contract and popularity make a deal less likely.

stories.t: Clayface leads Friday’s box office as a Nathan Fielder documentary expands
stories.s: DC’s Clayface took in about $10.4 million on Friday, including previews, and is on track for about $24 million this weekend. You Can See Everything, the documentary from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim about Elizabeth Holmes in the month before her prison sentence, grew to 2,655 theaters and earned $6.1 million. The stop-motion film Wildwood, voiced by Carey Mulligan and Jacob Tremblay, was third.

stories.t: Full moon, ‘Demon Star,’ and Halloween fireballs: what to see in the sky this week
stories.s: The full moon on Oct. 26 is the best time to see the bright streaks around the Tycho and Copernicus craters, even with binoculars. Algol, the “Demon Star,” dims noticeably every few days, and slow, bright Taurid meteors can show up after dark, with the shower peaking in early November. The Pleiades rise in the east before midnight.

stories.t: Galaxy-sized black holes can’t explain dark matter, study finds
stories.s: Physicists in Germany and Abu Dhabi used the leftover glow of the early universe to show that black holes bigger than whole galaxies can’t make up much of dark matter, since they would have left the glow looking grainy. The team is now testing whether much smaller, asteroid-mass black holes could fill the gap. The work is due in Physical Review Letters.

stories.t: Tankers burn near Hormuz as US–Iran tensions rise before the midterms
stories.s: Iran says seven oil tankers were set on fire or damaged in and around the Strait of Hormuz, and its Revolutionary Guard warned that new US strikes could bring a wider response. Analysts see a US attack before the Nov. 3 midterms as unlikely, but rhetoric on both sides keeps rising. Brent crude traded around $114 a barrel, up from about $72 before the war began in February.
stories.w: Oil near $114 keeps gas prices high for Bay Area drivers and adds to the cost of everything shipped in.

stories.t: Bay Area transit tax on the Nov. 3 ballot would decide BART and Caltrain cuts
stories.s: The Regional Transit Measure would add a half-cent sales tax in San Mateo, Alameda, Contra Costa, and Santa Clara counties and a one-cent tax in San Francisco for 14 years starting in April 2027, raising about $980 million a year for BART, Caltrain, Muni, and others. It needs a simple majority across the five counties. If it fails, BART could start closing low-ridership stations as early as January, and Caltrain faces major cuts.
stories.w: Millbrae’s BART and Caltrain station is a major hub, so the vote shapes both your sales tax and how often trains run on the Peninsula.

stories.t: Measure U would take San Mateo County’s district maps away from the supervisors
stories.s: Measure U would create an independent commission to draw the county’s five supervisor districts after each census, ending the board’s final say. Supporters point to 2021, when the board passed over a citizen panel’s maps and kept lines close to the old ones. No argument against it was filed, and ballots are due Nov. 3.
stories.w: District lines decide which supervisor represents Millbrae and how its voice is weighed on county issues.

stories.t: San Francisco declares a local emergency to prepare for El Niño storms
stories.s: Mayor Daniel Lurie declared a local emergency so city departments, including SFO, Muni, and Public Works, can buy flood barriers, pumps, and generators faster ahead of a possibly record-breaking El Niño winter. The city is preparing for coastal flooding, power outages, and damage to public buildings. Public Works offers up to 10 free sandbags per address.
stories.w: The same storms will hit the Peninsula, and SFO is on the list of agencies getting ready, so delays and outages are worth planning for now.

stories.t: Millbrae tests payment options as downtown paid parking takes shape
stories.s: The city’s downtown parking plan would add paid parking on the busiest blocks and could expand residential permits within a quarter mile of them. Residents tried out payment options at drop-in sessions on Thursday. Rates, hours, zones, and equipment are still undecided and will go to future City Council meetings, and a garage on one of three city lots is only being studied.
stories.w: Paid spaces downtown would change what errands and dining cost, and the council meetings ahead are the place to weigh in.

stories.t: American Express to cut about 3,500 jobs despite a 28% jump in profit
stories.s: The card company will trim roughly 5% of its workforce, its first large round of cuts in about a decade, even after third-quarter profit rose to $3.71 billion. Leadership called it an efficiency push, not a response to weaker business. It did not say which teams or locations will be affected.
stories.w: Even profitable companies are trimming staff, a sign of a cooler job market for Bay Area office workers.
stories.src: Associated Press via KPRC Click2Houston, Oct 23, 2026

stories.t: Newsom’s office says California homicides fell to their lowest level since 1966
stories.s: Visiting San Quentin for its film festival, Gov. Gavin Newsom’s office reported that homicides fell 18.6% from 2024 to 2025, with robbery down about 20% and car theft down about 26%. It also cited lower reoffending rates for people who complete rehabilitation programs and announced new funding for prison education and job training. The figures come from the governor’s office.
stories.w: Statewide drops in car theft and robbery tend to show up in local numbers too, which matters for Peninsula drivers and shop owners.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors fall to Memphis; 49ers play in Atlanta Sunday
stories.s: Warriors: lost 111–108 to the Grizzlies on Friday at Chase Center; Stephen Curry scored 24, and Memphis’s Ty Jerome had 28. 49ers: at the Falcons on Sunday, Oct. 25. Giants: in their off-season, with no major moves this week. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta short on healthy receivers
stories.s: San Francisco is 6–0 and can enter its bye at 7–0 with a win at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mike Evans is likely out or limited, Christian Kirk is expected to debut after a calf strain, and Nick Bosa may see a lighter workload. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris faces the team that fired him as head coach in January.

stories.t: DC’s Clayface opens with $3.5 million in previews and strong reviews
stories.s: The DC Studios body-horror film, directed by James Watkins from a script co-written by Mike Flanagan, earned about $3.5 million from Thursday previews. Projections for its domestic opening weekend range from $20 million to $30 million on a reported $44 million budget. It is Certified Fresh at 77% on Rotten Tomatoes.

stories.t: New this weekend: Yaga on AMC+, Newlyweds on NBC, and NBA on Prime returns
stories.s: AMC+ premiered the horror series Yaga with two episodes, and NBC launched the comedy Newlyweds alongside the season 3 return of Happy’s Place. Prime Video opened its second season of NBA games with a doubleheader, and Apple TV’s Dark Matter aired its next-to-last episode.

stories.t: Anderson .Paak and Cordae’s joint album Heavy Is the Crown earns an 8/10
stories.s: Clash calls the duo’s first collaborative album thoughtful, singling out tracks including the single “A Good Day,” the title track “Crown,” and the closer “Godfather 2.” The review credits .Paak for setting up Cordae from the opener onward.

stories.t: NASA lays out a faster Artemis plan aimed at a 2028 Moon landing
stories.s: At Kennedy Space Center, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and agency leaders outlined how they plan to speed up Artemis toward a crewed landing in 2028. Under the plan, Artemis III sends four astronauts to low Earth orbit next year to test systems needed for landing, and Artemis IV becomes the first mission to touch down.

stories.t: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, an AI agent that works while your app is closed
stories.s: Anthropic began inviting US Pro and Max subscribers from a waitlist to Claude Duet, a research preview that scans email and calendar each morning and keeps working in its own cloud environment. It pauses for approval before payments, signatures, or deletions, and it shares the plan’s usage limits.

stories.t: Meta pauses Muse chat sharing after thousands of shared links were found online
stories.s: Researchers found more than 6,000 shared Meta Muse conversations because each link carried the chat’s title, and some held loan applications and internal business reports. Meta switched off sharing while it fixes how links can be discovered. The lesson for any AI tool: share a summary instead of the full chat, and review links you’ve already shared.

stories.t: Voters will decide a $7.5 billion science research bond in 2028
stories.s: New since Thursday’s wrap-up: Newsom’s last signature of the session, made atop the Golden Gate Bridge, went on SB 895, which asks voters in March 2028 to approve a $7.5 billion bond for a state foundation funding peer-reviewed scientific and health research. In his final session he signed more than 1,000 bills and vetoed 120, for about 8,000 signed over eight years; he leaves office in January and says he may still call special sessions.
stories.w: Bay Area universities, hospitals and the South San Francisco biotech cluster would be among the biggest competitors for the research money if voters approve it.

stories.t: Pentagon creates a new command for autonomous drones and robots
stories.s: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star command, called AutoWarCom, to rapidly expand the military’s use of autonomous drones and robots. He also said the Pentagon will cut 20% of its generals and admirals.
stories.w: Bay Area tech and robotics companies could see new defense work from the push, along with renewed debate over military uses of AI built in Silicon Valley.

stories.t: Judge to review the secret legal basis for military boat strikes
stories.s: A federal judge will examine the Pentagon’s secret legal justification for its lethal strikes on boats, which have killed more than 200 people. After reviewing it, the judge will decide whether the reasoning should be made public.
stories.w: Californians following the military’s expanding use of force could learn how the government justifies the strikes, a question that may shape oversight debates in Congress.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers lead the NFC West as Warriors train in Hawaii
stories.s: The 49ers sit alone atop the NFC West at 3-0 after last Sunday’s 36-30 win over Arizona and host the Broncos this Sunday at 1:25 p.m. at Levi’s Stadium. The Warriors are midway through training camp at BYU–Hawaii, which runs through Saturday, ahead of Sunday’s preseason opener against the Clippers in Honolulu. The Earthquakes are idle until Oct. 10, and the Giants are in their offseason.

stories.t: Kerr installs a five-out offense at Warriors camp
stories.s: Steve Kerr used the first practice in Laie to install a five-out offense, saying the Warriors must keep up with how the league has changed after years of playing two big men. He plans to keep Steph Curry and Draymond Green together in the starting lineup and would like Al Horford off the bench for 18 to 20 minutes, but Kristaps Porziņģis didn’t travel to Hawaii and is out indefinitely with a health issue.

stories.t: New this weekend: Verity and Digger hit theaters, plus Miranda Lambert’s disco turn
stories.s: In theaters, Amazon MGM’s Verity with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson is tracking for $35 million or more and the No. 1 spot, while Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Digger, starring Tom Cruise, is projected at $12 million to $15 million against a $125 million budget. On streaming, Netflix’s seven-part East of Eden with Florence Pugh and HBO’s legal drama War with Dominic West and Sienna Miller premiered Thursday. New albums out today include Miranda Lambert’s Crisco, Victoria Monét’s Frequency of Love and Johnny Marr’s The Age of Everything, and the Hardly Strictly Bluegrass festival plays Golden Gate Park this weekend.

stories.t: Miranda Lambert goes country-disco on new album Crisco
stories.s: Lambert’s 11th album, out today on MCA Nashville, blends country with late-’70s and early-’80s disco strings across 12 tracks. It features Ella Langley on opener “Snakeskin Boots,” Chris Stapleton on “A Song to Sing” and a cover of Jim Croce’s “I’ll Have to Say I Love You in a Song”; RIFF gave it 8 out of 10, calling it a fun showcase of a veteran at ease.

stories.t: Crew-13 docks at the space station
stories.s: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 11:10 a.m. EDT Thursday, its first stage landed back at the Cape, and the Dragon docked to the station’s Harmony module at 7 p.m. EDT. NASA’s Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canada’s Joshua Kutryk and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov floated aboard after the hatch opened at 9:19 p.m., joining the seven-member Expedition 75 crew.

stories.t: Microsoft-linked data center ran gas generators without permits, report finds
stories.s: An investigation found that a Microsoft-linked data center in Vineland, New Jersey, ran dozens of gas-fired generators without permits for nearly a year, releasing large amounts of smog-forming pollution. The finding adds to questions about how the rush to build computing capacity for AI and cloud services is being powered.

stories.t: Newsom wraps up his last bill-signing season as governor
stories.s: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed and vetoed his last bills as governor by Wednesday’s deadline, working through a final batch of 1,160 measures and nearly 8,000 over his time in office. New laws include a 13-bill youth online safety package that bars social media companies from offering addictive features such as infinite scroll to users under 16, a ban on child marriage, stronger state antitrust powers, tax credits for local news outlets and a ban on public officials issuing crypto meme coins.
stories.w: Peninsula families with teens will see new limits on how social apps can hook kids, and struggling local newsrooms that cover San Mateo County could tap the new tax credits.

stories.t: Bay Area warm spell could last into mid-October
stories.s: Above-normal temperatures that arrived Tuesday are expected to hang on, with the 70s in San Francisco and the mid-80s to 90s inland, and a National Weather Service forecaster said the warmth could run into the middle of October. The coast should stay in the 60s and low 70s, and fire danger will be elevated, though strong winds aren’t in the forecast. San Francisco could see its first October streak of 10 straight 70-degree days since 2015.
stories.w: Bayside and inland Peninsula neighborhoods should expect warm afternoons for days: drink water, check on heat-sensitive neighbors and avoid anything that could spark a fire.

stories.t: Supreme Court lets third-country deportations resume for now
stories.s: On Tuesday the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to keep deporting people to countries other than their own while the justices decide whether migrants must first get a meaningful chance to object. The order pauses an appeals court ruling that federal attorneys said had forced the cancellation of a flight carrying about 70 people. The administration has sent about 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries, most of them to Mexico.
stories.w: San Mateo County is home to many immigrant families, and relatives facing removal could be sent to countries where they have no ties while the case plays out.

stories.t: Last U.S. troops leave Iraq, ending the anti-ISIS mission there
stories.s: The Pentagon said the last U.S. troops deployed for the fight against ISIS have left Iraq, departing Erbil Air Base in the Kurdistan region with their equipment. The task force has moved to Jordan, hundreds of U.S. troops remain in Syria, and the U.S. will keep offering training and intelligence support. Kurdish officials warned the pullout leaves their region exposed to Iranian strikes and a possible ISIS comeback.
stories.w: It closes a chapter that began in 2003 and touched many California military families, while U.S. forces in Jordan and Syria stay close to tensions with Iran.

stories.t: Today in sports: unbeaten 49ers turn to Denver
stories.s: The 49ers are 3-0 and alone atop the NFC West after Sunday’s 36-30 win over Arizona, when Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns; Denver visits Levi’s Stadium this Sunday at 1:25 p.m. on CBS. The Warriors opened training camp at BYU–Hawaii in Laie this week ahead of their preseason opener against the Clippers on Sunday in Honolulu. The Earthquakes beat Portland 3-1 on Saturday and next play Oct. 10, while the Giants’ season is over.

stories.t: Giants stand by Vitello after a 97-loss season
stories.s: Buster Posey gave manager Tony Vitello a vote of confidence after a first season that ended with 97 losses and the Giants missing the playoffs for the ninth time in 10 years. Posey took the blame for a bullpen that blew 27 saves and said adding dependable relievers is the top offseason priority; the team also expects Randy Rodríguez back from Tommy John surgery next season.

stories.t: Tom Cruise’s Digger splits critics ahead of Friday’s opening
stories.s: Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s oil-industry satire, starring Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell alongside John Goodman and Riz Ahmed, sat at 53% on Rotten Tomatoes as reviews rolled in. BBC Culture praised it as an art-house spectacle, while IndieWire likened it to a big-budget Dr. Strangelove riff that feels cut off from real human truth. It opens in theaters Friday.

stories.t: Early Verity review calls the Colleen Hoover thriller a twisty, fun ride
stories.s: Michael Showalter’s adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s best-seller stars Dakota Johnson as a broke writer hired to ghostwrite a famous author’s series, and Anne Hathaway as the injured novelist whose remote Vermont home hides a disturbing confession. Time Out gave it three of five stars, calling it a mostly fun ride that still piles on one twist too many. It opens in theaters Friday.

stories.t: SpaceX Crew-13 set to launch to the space station this morning
stories.s: NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins (commander) and Luke Delaney (pilot), Canada’s Joshua Kutryk and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov are scheduled to lift off at 11:10 a.m. EDT (8:10 a.m. Pacific) on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral. Forecasters gave a 55% chance of acceptable weather, with scattered showers possible, and NASA will stream the launch and docking.

stories.t: California adds new AI rules for workplaces, health care and deepfakes
stories.s: Newsom signed 13 AI bills on Wednesday: employers can’t rely only on AI to discipline or fire workers, must disclose when AI drives a mass layoff, and can’t put surveillance tools in workplace bathrooms. Other laws protect doctors’ judgment when AI tools are used in care, bar stripping digital watermarks from AI content, and require gene synthesis companies to screen orders, including Peninsula legislators’ bills SB 1000 (Sen. Josh Becker) and AB 1864 (Asm. Marc Berman).
